nodes.description: Absence of both HSJ1 isoforms: HSJ1a (277 aa, cytosolic and nuclear) and HSJ1b (324 aa, geranylgeranyl-anchored to the cytoplasmic face of the endoplasmic reticulum, the predominant isoform in neurons). Each carries an N-terminal J domain that binds HSP70 and stimulates its ATPase activity, and two C-terminal ubiquitin-interacting motifs that bind polyubiquitin chains and the proteasome. Loss of the protein therefore removes an HSP70 ATPase activator, an HSP70-binding client-delivery factor and a polyubiquitin-binding adaptor at once. Expression is highest in neurons, which fits the neural restriction of the disease.
